title: Am I not your Lord? Every soul once answered yes.
subtitle: The covenant taken before anyone was born

row.title: Yes, we testify
sub: so no one can say I forgot

then: Allah brought Adam's descendants out and made them testify that He is their Lord. Ibn Kathir links this to the fitrah in 30:30 and the hadith that {idea}every child is born upon the fitrah{/idea}. The reason is given: so no one can say on the Day of Resurrection, we were unaware.
now: Sometimes, in a quiet moment, on a night drive or holding a newborn, something in you reaches for Allah without being taught. {reward}That pull is the old yes.{/reward} It was there before any lesson.
old: Faith is something I have to build from nothing.
new: I already said yes to Allah once, and my heart remembers.
try: Sit for one quiet minute tonight and say: Bala, You are my Lord.

title: Our fathers did it is not an excuse.
subtitle: Inherited habits do not cancel your own covenant

row.title: we just followed
sub: will You punish us for them?

row.title: my upbringing
sub: it is how I was raised

then: The covenant was taken so people could not say on the Day: {trap}it was our fathers who took partners with Allah, we were only their descendants{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says each person testified for themselves, so the excuse of following the elders falls away.
now: My family always did it this way. Everyone in my town does it. It is cultural. These are real pressures. {idea}But each of us said our own yes{/idea}, and each of us answers for our own choices.
old: I cannot be blamed for what I was raised with.
new: My upbringing explains me, but I still answer for my own choices.
try: Name one habit you inherited. Ask honestly: would I choose this if I were starting fresh?

title: The signs are spelled out so that they might return.
subtitle: Detail given for one purpose: coming back
then: After reminding people of the covenant, Allah says: thus do We explain the verses in detail, {idea}so that they may turn back{/idea}. The long stories of this surah all serve this purpose: to bring people back to the yes they once gave.
now: You have read this surah's stories before: Fir'awn, the calf, the Sabbath town. Easy to treat them as history. {idea}They are written so you return.{/idea} Each one is a door back home.
old: These stories are about people long ago.
new: Every detail Allah explains is an invitation for me to return.
try: Pick one story from this surah. Ask: where is the way back for me in it?

title: Given the signs, he slipped out of them like a skin.
subtitle: A man of knowledge who walked away from it

row.title: I know, so I am safe

then: Ibn Mas'ud and others said this is about Bal'am bin Ba'ura, a man given knowledge of Allah's signs. Malik bin Dinar reported that {trap}a king gave him land and gifts, and he left the religion of Musa{/trap}. Ibn 'Abbas said his people kept pressing him to pray against Musa until he did.
now: You know the hadiths. You can quote the ayat. Then a job offer comes that needs you to bend one rule, and then another. {trap}Knowledge does not protect you by itself.{/trap} It can be peeled off, one gift at a time.
old: Because I know so much about the deen, I am safe.
new: Knowledge I do not live by can be stripped away.
try: Take one thing you know well about Islam. Act on it today, in a way no one sees.

title: He could have been raised, but he clung to the ground.
subtitle: The parable of the panting dog
then: Allah could have raised him by those signs, {trap}but he clung to the earth and followed his desires{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says he was drawn by the adornment of this life. One meaning of the parable: like a dog that pants whether chased or left alone, {trap}advice never reached him{/trap}. The verse ends: relate the stories, perhaps they will think.
now: A raise, then a bigger car, then a bigger house, and the restlessness never stops. Push yourself or rest, it is the same breathless feeling. {idea}Clinging to the ground keeps you panting.{/idea}
old: Once I get a bit more, I will finally feel settled.
new: Clinging to this world keeps me restless whatever I get.
try: Skip one purchase or upgrade you were planning this week. Notice how it feels.

title: An evil example, and the harm landed on themselves.
subtitle: The ones who rejected the signs wronged only their own souls
then: The verse closes the story of the man who abandoned Allah's signs. {trap}How evil is the example of those who reject the signs{/trap}, and the verse says it plainly: {trap}they used to wrong themselves{/trap}.
now: You stop praying, skip the Quran, drift away from the mosque friends. Allah is not smaller for it. {trap}You are.{/trap} The restlessness, the shorter temper, the empty Sunday evenings: that is the cost, and you are the one paying it.
old: Leaving the deen only matters to religious people.
new: Turning from Allah's signs only wrongs my own soul.
try: Bring back one small act of worship you dropped. Do it once today.

title: Whoever Allah guides is truly guided.
subtitle: Guidance is His to give, so ask Him for it
then: After the story of a learned man who lost his way, the verse says whom Allah guides is the guided one. Ibn Kathir cites the opening words the Prophet ﷺ used, reported by Ibn Mas'ud: {idea}whom Allah guides, none can mislead; whom He misguides, none can guide{/idea}.
now: You have read the books, watched the lectures, argued the points. Still you know people smarter than you who drifted away. {idea}Guidance is not a skill you master.{/idea} It is a gift you keep asking for, seventeen times a day in al-Fatiha.
old: If I learn enough, I will stay on the right path.
new: Guidance is Allah's gift, so I keep asking for it humbly.
try: In your next prayer, say ihdinas-siratal-mustaqim slowly and mean it as a request.

title: Hearts that do not understand, eyes that do not see.
subtitle: Having senses and not using them for guidance
then: The verse speaks soberly of those headed for Hell: they have hearts, eyes and ears they do not use for guidance. Ibn Kathir cites 22:46: {trap}it is not the eyes that grow blind, but the hearts in the chests{/trap}. Cattle at least answer their shepherd's call; these did not.
now: You watched three hours of videos today and heard nothing that moved you. Your eyes passed over the sunset and saw only traffic. {idea}The senses work fine.{/idea} The question is whether they are taking anything in for the heart.
old: I see and hear everything around me.
new: My senses were given to lead me to Allah, not just to fill my day.
try: Today, look at one thing in nature for one full minute and think of who made it.

title: To Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call Him by them.
subtitle: Calling on Allah by the names that fit your need
then: Allah's names are the most beautiful, and believers are told to call Him by them. Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet ﷺ teaching a dua for grief that asks Allah {reward}by every name He has{/reward}. Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said deviating in His names included naming idols like Al-Lat from Allah's name.
now: You are sitting in the hospital car park. Instead of just please, you say: {reward}Ya Shafi, Ya Rahim.{/reward} Lost money: Ya Razzaq. A wrong you did: Ya Ghafur. Each name is a door matched to the need.
old: Dua is just asking for what I want.
new: Calling Allah by the name that fits my need makes my dua more alive.
try: Pick one name of Allah that fits your biggest worry. Use it in your dua tonight.

title: There will always be some who guide by truth.
subtitle: A community that keeps to truth and justice
then: After describing the heedless, Allah says there is a community that guides by truth and establishes justice. Ibn Kathir notes reports that this refers to the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ, and cites the hadith: {reward}there will always be a group of my Ummah apparent on the truth, unharmed by those who oppose them{/reward}.
now: After reading the news, it can feel like everyone has lost their way. {reward}But somewhere a teacher is staying late for a struggling student. A judge is refusing a bribe.{/reward} Look for them, and try to be one.
old: Everyone is corrupt, so what difference can I make?
new: There are always people standing on truth, and I can be among them.
try: Find one person living with integrity near you. Thank them, or learn from them, this week.

title: Step by step, led on from where they do not notice.
subtitle: When ease becomes a trap

row.title: Allah is pleased
sub: look how well I am doing

then: Those who reject Allah's signs are led on gradually from where they do not perceive. Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}the doors of provision are opened for them, and they are deceived into thinking they are on the right path{/trap}. He cites 6:44, where the gates of everything opened just before the end.
now: You stopped praying months ago, and since then work has gone great: the promotion, the bonus, the new flat. It is tempting to think it does not matter. {idea}Success while far from Allah is not a sign of His approval.{/idea}
old: If life is going well, I must be doing something right.
new: Ease while I ignore Allah may be drawing me further away, step by step.
try: On your next good day, check yourself: am I closer to Allah than last month, or further?

title: I give them time, and My plan is firm.
subtitle: Delay is not escape
then: Following the last verse, Allah says He gives them time, and {idea}His plan is firm{/idea}. Ibn Kathir explains it as prolonging what they are in, while the plan stays strong and perfect.
now: You did something wrong years ago and nothing came of it. It is easy to forget it, as if it never happened. {idea}The time you have been given is not proof you got away.{/idea} {reward}It is the space to turn back.{/reward}
old: Nothing bad happened, so it must not have mattered.
new: Allah's respite is time given to repent, not proof I escaped.
try: Think of an old wrong you have never repented from. Repent today, and fix what you can.
